# Road safety audit: FI 20250530_video-1

Source: SAM 3.1 tiled video tracking (Meta Model API). Observed 8.9 min; 321 two-wheelers, 303 vehicles. Traffic control: Signalized; right turns signal-controlled: no.

Conflicts: 222 interacting pairs with PET ≤ 1.5 s or TTC ≤ 1.5 s (152 PET, 70 TTC). Each pair is counted once, by PET when it has one.

Hotspots are 15 m cells ranked by the lower bound of the exact Poisson 95% interval on conflicts per 1,000 road users through the cell (at least 2 conflicts). These are surrogate measures from a short observation, not crash frequencies.

## Hotspot 1 at (7.5, -7.5) m

33 conflicts among 195 road users: 169.2 per 1,000 (95% CI 116.5–237.7). Dominant: 20 crossing vehicle – vehicle conflicts (min PET 0.3 s; min TTC 0.7 s; movements 9 left, 5 unknown, 8 through, 3 right; signal on entry (vehicles) 14 green, 2 yellow, 1 red).

Muse Spark reviewed the video of the 3 most severe of these: 2 judged real conflicts, 1 not (2 with visible braking or swerving).

Illustration: Dedicated Left- and Right-Turn Lanes at Intersections (hotspot1_20250530_video-1.png). SAM 3.1 check for 'arrow road marking' in the hotspot: found (covered share 0.004 before, 0.092 after). AI-generated; not an engineering design.

| FHWA Proven Safety Countermeasure | CMF Clearinghouse ID | CMF | Crash reduction | Rating | Crash type | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Backplates with Retroreflective Borders | 1447 | 0.50 | 50% | not rated | Angle |  |
| Dedicated Left- and Right-Turn Lanes at Intersections | 276 | 0.74 | 26% | 4★ | Angle |  |
| Reduced Left-Turn Conflict Intersections | 10870 | 0.61 | 39% | 5★ | Angle |  |
| Yellow Change Intervals | 4218 | 0.84 | 16% | 3★ | Angle |  |

Considered and rejected:

- Crosswalk Visibility Enhancements: targets pedestrian crashes; no pedestrian in this conflict
- Leading Pedestrian Interval: targets pedestrian crashes; no pedestrian in this conflict
- Medians and Pedestrian Refuge Islands in Urban and Suburban Areas: targets pedestrian crashes; no pedestrian in this conflict
- Pedestrian Hybrid Beacons: applies to Uncontrolled sites, not Signalized
- Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons: applies to Uncontrolled sites, not Signalized
- Walkways: targets pedestrian crashes; no pedestrian in this conflict
- Corridor Access Management: requires driveway or access-point conflicts, which the observed conflicts do not show
- Roundabouts: no reducing CMF rated >= 3 stars or unrated
- Systemic Application of Multiple Low-Cost Countermeasures at Stop-Controlled Intersections: applies to Stop-controlled sites, not Signalized
- Yellow Change Intervals: 2 CMFs for this crash type show no reduction (CMF ≥ 1; IDs 4210, 4222)
- Lighting: requires nighttime, which the observed conflicts do not show
- Pavement Friction Management: requires wet or low-friction pavement, which the observed conflicts do not show

## Hotspot 2 at (-7.5, -37.5) m

13 conflicts among 70 road users: 185.7 per 1,000 (95% CI 98.9–317.6). Dominant: 8 turning vehicle – vehicle conflicts (min PET 0.0 s; movements 4 right, 3 unknown, 1 left, 2 through, 2 u-turn; signal on entry (vehicles) 3 green).

panel.memo:
# Memo: Signalized Intersection Conflict Review

## What was observed
In 535.1 observed seconds, the highest-priority hotspot had 33 events and a rate of 169.2 per 1000 users. Its dominant pattern was vehicle–vehicle crossing with 20 events, minimum PET 0.3, left movement 9, entry signal G 14 with y 2 and r 1. Video review covered 3 events: 2 were real and 2 involved evasive braking/yielding.

Elsewhere, evidence was weaker: one turning hotspot had right 4 versus left 1 and only 1 real event in 3 reviewed; one rear_end hotspot had 0 real events in 3 reviewed, judged normal car-following.

## Countermeasures to consider first
Consider **CMF 10870** first: converting to a median U-turn addresses the left-turn crossing pattern and has CMF 0.6108 for Angle crashes. Also consider **CMF 4218**: increasing the total change interval addresses entries on yellow/red, with CMF 0.84 for Angle crashes, but the y 2 and r 1 counts make this secondary to the left-turn pattern.

Do not advance the rank 2 or rank 3 MUT proposals on current evidence.

## Limits
These are surrogate measures from a short observation, not crash predictions. Rates have wide uncertainty, video review samples are small, and artefacts/false conflicts were found. A qualified traffic engineer must review any design, signal timing, access, and feasibility before implementation.
